conventions.convention: The sample has n ≥ 1 and p ≥ 1. Left branches use x_j ≤ t, right branches use x_j > t, and both child sample sets must be nonempty.
Regression leaves predict sample means. Classification leaves predict the most frequent class, choosing the least class index in a tie. Entropy uses natural logarithms and 0 log 0 = 0.
R(T) is total sample-count-weighted leaf impurity, |T| counts leaves, and C_α(T) = R(T) + α|T| for α ≥ 0. The weakest-link denominator is |T_t| − 1.
The root has depth zero. Candidate thresholds are adjacent-distinct-value midpoints; score ties use coordinate index then cut index. Splits need no strictly positive loss reduction.
Pruning recomputes quotients on the current tree, collapses one minimizing node per iteration, and resolves ties by lexicographic root-to-node address with L < R.

load_bearing.statement: Finite empirical binary trees split sample indices using coordinate thresholds with two nonempty children; terminal sample sets partition the sample. Regression predictions are leaf means; classification predictions and impurities follow the specified class-frequency rules.

Let I be a nonempty finite set of sample indices and let y_i be real for every i ∈ I. Among all real constants c, the unique minimizer of Σ_i(y_i − c)² is the sample mean, and the minimum value is the sum of squared deviations from that mean.

Under the greedy CART input conditions, each selected split minimizes the declared child-weighted empirical loss among all nonempty coordinate-threshold partitions, with the specified tie rule. Growth terminates with depth at most the maximum depth and nonempty children at every split; no global tree optimality is asserted.
For collapsed subtrees of a fixed finite empirical tree, define R(T) as total training impurity, C_α(T) = R(T) + α|T| for α ≥ 0, and g(t) = [R(t) − R(T_t)]/(|T_t| − 1) for current nonterminal nodes.

published_dependencies.used_for: The node-mean proof equips the real scalar domain and finite coordinate codomain with standard inner products before applying the normal-equation theorem.
The node-mean proof verifies directly that summing coordinates is the adjoint of the constant-vector embedding.
The node-mean proof applies the finite-dimensional minimizer characterization T*(Tc − b) = 0; all required linearity and inner-product hypotheses are established.

concerns.concern: Verification 3.1 says, “The root split has depth $1=d_{\max}$”. The algorithm assigns the root depth 0; its children have depth 1 and therefore remain leaves. The computed output is correct, but this sentence misidentifies the node depths.

seams_checked.note: The forest algorithm preserves nonempty bootstrap-position child sets, midpoint candidates, weighted impurity scores, depth-zero roots, depth caps, and deterministic ties. It explicitly identifies m = p with CART and m < p with nodewise coordinate restriction. CART suppliers assert no forest performance guarantee. Its data-flow diagram agrees with the construction.

Gradient boosting fits finite-depth squared-error CART to finite pseudo-residuals and uses its finite, nonempty leaf partition. It distinguishes fitted leaf means from subsequent line-minimizing offsets. The nonincreasing-loss theorem cites CART only for finite output and the sample partition; its inequality follows from attained leafwise minima and comparison with zero offsets.
